Event: Malouf Music Tradition | Year: 1500 CE | Location: Tunisia | Country: Tunisia | Type: Cultural Reform | Historical Figure: Andalusian Musicians

Description: Preserved malouf - Andalusian classical music brought by refugees. Complex rhythms, Arabic poetry, Mediterranean melodies. Malouf became Tunisia's classical music, performed at weddings, festivals, concerts.

First-Person Account: Malouf connected us to Andalusian golden age - when Muslims, Christians, Jews created culture together. Music preserved this memory. Every performance was nostalgia for lost convivencia.

Reflection on Mistakes: Malouf remained elite music, not popular. Most Tunisians preferred Egyptian pop. Classical music can't compete with mass culture. We preserved malouf in conservatories but it lost living context.

Modern Strategic Analysis: Modern classical music: everywhere struggles against popular music. Opera, malouf, gamelan - traditional high culture becomes museum pieces. Preservation through performance vs. living tradition. Can classical forms survive without ritual context?
